_documentation.purpose: Main flowers that customers can pick in the bouquet designer, with bundle and per-stem pricing.
conventions: Top level is an object with two keys: `_documentation` (this block, ignored by the app) and `items` (the array of records the app reads).
Prices are in Philippine pesos (PHP), stored as plain numbers with no currency symbol.
`null` means the value is not known yet. It never means zero. Check for null before doing math on a value.
Enumerated values (type, origin, occasion, mood, etc.) are lowercase, with hyphens instead of spaces where noted.
`id` values are unique and stable. Gaps in the numbering are fine, and ids should not be reused or renumbered.
`image` paths are served from the site root, so `/images/flowers/x.png` means the file `public/images/flowers/x.png`. The image files themselves have not been added yet.

fields.name: string. Display name, singular.
fields.family: string. Groups variants of the same flower so the designer can show one card (for example, `rose`) that opens to its variants. Equals the item's own lowercase name when it has no variants.
fields.type: string or null. One of: fresh, dried, paper, money, rubber, fuzzy wire, wood.
fields.description: string. Short two-sentence customer-facing description based on popular flower-language meanings. Empty for Sunlight until that flower is identified.
fields.stock: integer or null. 0 means out of stock, null means not counted yet.
fields.bundleSize: integer or null. Number of stems in one bundle. Roses and carnation are assumed to be 12 (a dozen) until confirmed.
fields.bundlePrice: object {min, max} or null. Regular price of one bundle. If min equals max it is a single price, otherwise a range. Anthurium has two price options (450 and 780), stored as min 450 and max 780.
fields.seasonalPrices: object. Season name mapped to a bundle price, for example {"undas": 650}. Empty object if there is none.
fields.price: number or null. Per-stem price used in the designer. Where bundleSize is known it is bundlePrice.max divided by bundleSize, rounded up to a whole peso. Null if bundleSize is unknown.
fields.occasion: array of up to 4 strings: up to 3 main occasions, plus `just-because` where the flower suits casual, everyday affection. Allowed values: anniversary, birthday, graduation, valentines, mothers-day, wedding, undas, funeral, get-well, congratulations, housewarming, just-because.
fields.mood: array of up to 3 strings. Allowed values: romantic, loving, sweet, passionate, elegant, graceful, cheerful, happy, playful, hopeful, grateful, peaceful, solemn, respectful, welcoming, joyful, fresh, warm, sentimental.
fields.color: array of strings. Colors the shop stocks, lowercase (for example, red, pink, white). Three common colors per item were added as a starting point, not confirmed stock. Replace them with the shop's actual stocked colors. Used by the designer's color search.
fields.active: boolean. `false` hides the item from the app (unfinished entries or placeholders). Inactive items stay in the file.

notes: Occasion and mood are general florist conventions adapted to the Philippine context, not sales data. Sunlight is left empty because the flower is not yet identified.
Gimba (Jimba) and Radus are chrysanthemum varieties, and Puto-puto is also a chrysanthemum variety, so they share the chrysanthemum's meanings.
How many stems a customer puts in a bouquet is chosen in the designer and saved with their design. It is not stored in this file.
Sunlight is inactive (`active: false`) because it is not yet identified and has no occasion, mood, or description.

Families: all rose entries share `rose`, the two calla lilies share `calla-lily`, Stargazer and Lily (Local) share `lily`, and the chrysanthemum varieties (Chrysanthemum, Colored Mum, Puto-puto, Ping Pong, Gimba, Radus) share `chrysanthemum`. Edit `family` to change how the designer groups cards.

items.name: Local Rose
items.description: Roses are a classic choice for expressing love, beauty, and admiration. Locally grown and affordable, they suit anniversaries, birthdays, and heartfelt surprises.

items.name: China Rose
items.description: China roses are a timeless symbol of deep love, passion, and appreciation. Their elegant blooms make a lasting impression on romantic occasions.

items.name: Ecuadorian Rose
items.description: Ecuadorian roses are prized for their large, long-lasting blooms and stand for devotion, luxury, and deep affection. They are a premium way to show someone they are truly treasured.

items.name: Cagayan Rose
items.description: Cagayan roses are a locally grown rose that carries the classic meaning of love and admiration. Their warm blooms suit sweet gestures as well as quiet remembrance.

items.name: Paper Rose
items.description: Paper roses never wilt, so they stand for love that lasts. They make a keepsake gift that keeps its beauty long after the occasion.

items.name: Calla Lily (Imported)
items.description: Calla lilies are a symbol of purity, elegance, and magnificent beauty. Their smooth, graceful shape makes them a favorite for weddings and anniversaries.

items.name: Calla Lily (Local)
items.description: Calla lilies stand for purity, grace, and faithful devotion. Locally grown, they bring a refined touch to weddings, anniversaries, and Mother's Day bouquets.

items.name: Tulip
items.description: Tulips are a symbol of perfect love and cheerful spring renewal. Their clean, simple blooms are a warm choice for birthdays and Mother's Day.

items.name: Stargazer
items.description: Stargazer lilies stand for ambition, prosperity, and passionate admiration. Their bold, fragrant blooms make a showy centerpiece for anniversaries and special celebrations.

items.name: Carnation
items.description: Carnations are a flower of gratitude and a mother's love, with deeper shades often meaning admiration. They are a long-time favorite for Mother's Day and are also offered during Undas as a sign of remembrance.

items.name: Gerbera
items.description: Gerberas stand for cheerfulness, innocence, and pure joy. Their bright, daisy-like faces are perfect for birthdays, graduations, and get-well wishes.

items.name: Sunflower
items.description: Sunflowers are a symbol of loyalty, adoration, and positivity. Their sunny blooms bring warmth to graduations, birthdays, and get-well gifts.

items.name: Anthurium
items.description: Anthuriums are a symbol of hospitality, happiness, and abundance. Their glossy, heart-shaped blooms are a bold gift for congratulations and housewarmings.

items.name: Gimba
items.description: Gimba (also spelled Jimba) is a chrysanthemum variety sold in bundles during Undas. Like other chrysanthemums, it stands for loyalty, friendship, and lasting remembrance.

items.name: Chrysanthemum
items.description: Chrysanthemums symbolize loyalty, friendship, and lasting remembrance. In the Philippines, they are a traditional Undas flower for honoring loved ones who have passed.

items.name: Colored Mum
items.description: Colored mums share the chrysanthemum's meaning of loyalty, friendship, and remembrance. Their bright shades add cheer to birthdays and graduations while remaining a familiar Undas flower.

items.name: Puto-puto
items.description: Puto-puto is a chrysanthemum variety grown in the Philippines and a familiar flower during Undas. It symbolizes remembrance and respect for loved ones who have passed.

items.name: Ping Pong
items.description: Ping pong mums stand for cheerfulness, friendship, and joy. Their round, playful blooms are a fun choice for birthdays, graduations, and congratulations.

items.name: Hydrangea
items.description: Hydrangeas are a symbol of gratitude, heartfelt emotion, and abundance. Their full, lush clusters make a graceful gift for weddings, anniversaries, and Mother's Day.

items.name: Radus
items.description: Radus is the local name for Malaysian mums, a chrysanthemum variety widely grown in Benguet. Chrysanthemums symbolize loyalty, friendship, and lasting remembrance, which is why radus is a staple of Undas and funeral flowers.

items.name: Lily (Local)
items.description: Lilies are a classic symbol of purity, devotion, and peace. They are often chosen for Undas and funerals to express respect and comfort, and they also suit Mother's Day.
